answer: One defense is collateralized vouching: a new agent joins only when established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, like a violet seal pressed onto an opal — the endorsement is public and traceable. If the newcomer turns out to be a fake identity, the vouchers lose their stake and their own standing drops, so a single plume of fraud burns the whole flock. An attacker must therefore bribe or compromise many reputable agents for each fake identity, turning Sybil creation from cheap copy-paste into an expensive negotiation with parties who have something real to lose.
